items.title: Section: Avoiding What Should Not Be Thought About

items.zh: 於自所證，離增上慢；於少下劣差別證中，不生喜足；於上所證中無退屈；善能遠離不應思處，時時修習止觀瑜伽，樂斷樂修，無間修習、殷重修習。
items.en: Regarding one's own realisation, one is free from overestimation; regarding a lesser, inferior degree of realisation, one does not become complacent; regarding a higher realisation yet to be attained, one does not lose heart. Skilfully avoiding what should not be thought about, one cultivates the yoga of calming and insight from time to time, delighting in cutting off the afflictions and delighting in cultivation, practising without interruption and with earnest seriousness.

items.title: Resting From Fatigue, Done Discreetly and Briefly

items.zh: 又於熱分極炎暑時，勇猛策勵，發勤精進，隨作一種所應作事，勞倦因緣，遂於非時發起惛睡。為此義故，暫應寢息，欲令惛睡疾疾除遣，勿經久時，損減善品、障礙善品。於寢息時，或關閉門，或令苾芻在傍看守，或毘奈耶隱密軌則，以衣蔽身，在深隱處須臾寢息，令諸勞睡皆悉除遣。如是名為正知而住先後次第。謂依行時及依住時。
items.en: Furthermore, during the hottest part of the hot season, having courageously exerted oneself in whatever task is called for, one may grow fatigued from the exertion and, though it is not the proper time, become drowsy. For this reason, one should briefly rest, so as to swiftly dispel the drowsiness — but not for long, lest it diminish or obstruct wholesome practice. While resting, one should close the door, or have a fellow monastic keep watch nearby, or, following the Vinaya's discreet provisions, cover the body with the robe and rest briefly in a secluded spot, so that the fatigue is fully dispelled. This is called the sequence of clear awareness in conduct, according to activity and according to dwelling.

items.title: Section: What "Clear Knowing" and "Abiding" Actually Mean

items.zh: 又於善品先未趣入，心興加行如理作意俱行妙慧，說名正知。即此正知，行時、住時，一切成辦無所減少，如是名為正知而住。
items.en: Furthermore, regarding wholesome states not yet entered into, the subtle wisdom that arises together with applied effort and correct attention is called clear knowing. This very clear knowing, whether in activity or in dwelling, accomplishing everything without any diminishment — this is called clear awareness in conduct.

items.zh: 當知此中，若往、若還、若覩、若瞻、若屈、若申、持僧伽胝及以衣鉢、若食、若飲、若噉、若甞正知而住，由是名為於村邑等如法行時正知而住。若行、若住、若坐、若臥、若習覺寤、若語、若默、若解勞睡正知而住，由是名為於其住處如法住時正知而住。如是應知已廣分別正知而住。復云何知此中略義？

items.title: Section: The Brief Summary — Five Activities, Five Dwellings, Four Governing Factors

items.zh: 謂於行時有五種業，於其住時有五種業，行時、住時正知而住有四種業，如是名為正知而住所有略義。云何行時有五種業？一者、身業，二者、眼業，三者、一切支節業，四者、衣鉢業，五者、飲食業。如是名為行時五業。謂若說言：若往、若還。此言顯示行時身業。若復說言：若覩、若瞻。此言顯示行時眼業。若復說言：若屈、若申。此言顯示行時一切支節業。若復說言：持僧伽胝及以衣鉢。此言顯示行時衣鉢業。若復說言：若食、若飲、若噉、若甞。此言顯示行時飲食業。云何名為住時五業？一者、身業，二者、語業，三者、意業，四者、晝業，五者、夜業。謂若說言：若行、若住、若坐。此言顯示住時身業。若復說言：若語。此言顯示住時語業。若復說言：若臥、若默、若解勞睡。此言顯示住時意業。若復說言：若習覺寤。此言顯示住時晝業、夜業、身業、語業。又若臥者，此言顯示住時夜業。當知是名住時五業。
items.en: There are five acts while active, five acts while dwelling, and four factors governing clear awareness in conduct whether active or dwelling — this is the brief summary of clear awareness in conduct. What are the five acts while active? First, the act of the body; second, the act of the eyes; third, the act of all the limbs; fourth, the act involving robe and bowl; fifth, the act of eating and drinking. What are the five acts while dwelling? First, the act of the body; second, the act of speech; third, the act of mind; fourth, the act of the day; fifth, the act of the night.

items.title: The Four Factors: Mindfulness, Correct Action, Freedom From Fault, Accumulated Provisions

items.zh: 云何名為行時、住時正知而住所有四業？謂初依彼行業、住業起如是業，即於彼業安守正念，不放逸住。當知此業，正念所攝、不放逸攝。若於是事、是處、是時，如量、如理、如其品類所應作者，即於此事、此處、此時，如量、如理、如其品類正知而作。彼由如是正知作故，於現法中無罪無犯，無有惡作，無變無悔；於當來世亦無有罪，身壞死後不墮惡趣，不生一切那落迦中。為得未得，積習資糧。如是名為正知而住所有略義。
items.en: What are the four factors governing clear awareness in conduct, whether active or dwelling? It means that, based on the acts of activity and dwelling just described, one gives rise to those very acts while firmly maintaining mindfulness and dwelling without negligence — know that these acts are comprised of mindfulness and of freedom from negligence [in activity and in dwelling alike, making four]. Regarding a given matter, place, and time, one acts exactly as is proper in measure, in reason, and in kind. Because one acts with such clear knowing, in this present life one is without fault, without transgression, without remorse, without inner corruption, and without regret; in the life to come, one is likewise without fault, and upon the body's dissolution at death, one does not fall into a miserable rebirth, nor is one born into any hell. And, for the sake of attaining what has not yet been attained, one accumulates the provisions for the path. This is the brief summary of clear awareness in conduct.

items.title: Section: Clear Awareness in Conduct Closes, and Fascicle 24 Reaches Its True End

items.zh: 前廣分別，今此略義，一切總名正知而住。
items.en: The detailed exposition given before, together with this brief summary given now, are all together called clear awareness in conduct.

blocks.text: The end of clear awareness in conduct, and of fascicle 24. One short passage (0416c11) is untranslated.
One avoids reflecting on the "inconceivable" matters, and does not claim attainments one lacks. Venerable Miào Jìng: "don't claim the first absorption when you haven't attained it."

Speech should be "measured, straight, and calm". Venerable Miào Jìng: not too much; without flattery; without agitation. Rest is brief and discreet: "cover the body with the robe and rest briefly in a secluded spot". Master Cháng Bǎi: a 須臾 is forty-eight minutes.

"Regarding wholesome states not yet entered, the subtle wisdom that arises with effort and correct attention is called clear knowing." "This clear knowing, whether in activity or dwelling, accomplishing everything without diminishment, is called clear awareness in conduct."

Five activities: of the body, the eyes, the limbs, robe and bowl, and eating. Five dwellings. Four governing factors: mindfulness, correct action, freedom from fault, and accumulated provisions. Master Cháng Bǎi: activity and dwelling each have two: what mindfulness covers and what non-negligence covers. Venerable Miào Jìng: 惡作 here also means changing one's mind and regretting it.

Wakefulness and clear awareness: the practice of the whole day and night. The next fascicle continues the provisions: good friendship, hearing and reflecting on the Dharma, freedom from obstacles, generosity, and the adornments of a renunciant.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng illustrate "free from overestimation" and "not complacent with lesser realisation"?
options: don't claim the first absorption without it; a small, inferior attainment is no cause for contentment
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: don't claim the first absorption when you haven't attained it — that is wrong; and if you have a small attainment, scanty and inferior, don't be content with it.

quiz.q: The English renders 言詞稱量 and 言詞正直 as "measured" and "orderly." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain them?
options: measured means not saying too much; straight means not flattering; calm means not too loud
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: measured speech means speaking in moderation, not too much; straight speech means no flattery or crookedness; calm speech means not too loud. The English "orderly" misses "not flattering."

quiz.q: When resting from fatigue "briefly," how long does Master Cháng Bǎi say a 須臾 is?
quiz.why: "Cover the body with the robe and rest briefly in a secluded spot, so that the fatigue is fully dispelled." Master Cháng Bǎi: a 須臾 is forty-eight minutes — a short time, just a brief rest.

quiz.q: What does the treatise call "clear knowing"?
options: the subtle wisdom that arises with effort and correct attention regarding wholesome states not yet entered
quiz.why: "Regarding wholesome states not yet entered into, the subtle wisdom that arises together with applied effort and correct attention is called clear knowing." Venerable Miào Jìng: clear knowing is wisdom, prepared before practice even begins.

quiz.q: Which factor of the eightfold path does Master Cháng Bǎi say "clear awareness in conduct" corresponds to?
quiz.why: "This very clear knowing, whether in activity or in dwelling, accomplishing everything without any diminishment — this is called clear awareness in conduct." Master Cháng Bǎi: the treatise's clear awareness in conduct is right action in the eightfold path.

quiz.q: What are the five acts while active?
options: body, eyes, all the limbs, robe and bowl, eating and drinking
quiz.why: "First, the act of the body; second, the act of the eyes; third, the act of all the limbs; fourth, the act involving robe and bowl; fifth, the act of eating and drinking." The five while dwelling are body, speech, mind, day, and night. Master Cháng Bǎi: going out, the eyes see many forms — that is the act of the eyes.

quiz.q: The English reads the "four factors" as four separate items, First … Second … How do the lectures, following the commentary, read them?
options: activity and dwelling each have two — what mindfulness covers and what non-negligence covers — making four
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: activity and dwelling each have two — what mindfulness covers and what non-negligence covers — four in all. Venerable Miào Jìng: activity includes maintaining mindfulness and non-negligence, and so does dwelling. The English and its note follow Kuījī's reading, counting proper action, faultlessness, and provisions as separate factors.
